title: Structural Organisation in Animals
seo_title: Structural Organisation in Animals Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 7: Structural Organisation in Animals
standard_text: Animal tissues; morphology, anatomy and functions of different systems (digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous and reproductive) of an insect (cockroach) and frog (brief account only).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7 Structural Organisation in Animals: epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissues, cell junctions, and the frog. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Four animal tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular, neural.
key_sub: Structure suits function in every tissue.
body_html:
How to think about it

Epithelia cover surfaces and line cavities: squamous, cuboidal, columnar, ciliated and compound. Connective tissues (areolar, adipose, tendon, ligament, cartilage, bone, blood) support and link other tissues. Muscle may be skeletal, smooth or cardiac, and neural tissue carries impulses. Cells are linked by tight, adhering and gap junctions.

The frog (Rana tigrina) is cold-blooded, breathes through its skin in water, has a three-chambered heart, excretes urea and has external fertilisation with a tadpole stage.

Example

Tissue lining air sacs?

thin, flat

Answer: squamous epithelium

Example

Frog heart chambers?

2 atria, 1 ventricle

Answer: 3

Common mistakes

  • Calling blood an epithelium.
  • Mixing up tendons and ligaments.
  • Saying the frog has a four-chambered heart.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
faq.a: A tendon joins muscle to bone; a ligament joins bone to bone.

faq.q: How does a frog breathe in water?
faq.a: Through its moist skin, which is richly supplied with blood vessels.
